name: ldapvi
desc: Update LDAP entries with a text editor
why: Editing live LDAP directory entries in a text editor is a neat door into a protocol most developers only meet through identity systems.

brief.what_it_is: ldapvi is an interactive LDAP client for Unix terminals. You point it at an LDAP directory, it pulls entries into a text editor, and you change them there. When you save, the edits are written back to the server. The homepage compares it to vipw(1) for LDAP.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents it as a way to update LDAP entries with a text editor, framed as vipw(1) for LDAP.
brief.standout: It treats live directory entries like a file you edit in your own editor, in the spirit of vipw(1), instead of requiring a dedicated admin GUI or a long series of LDAP command-line operations.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage lists tarball ldapvi-1.8.tar.gz, with older versions 1.0 through 1.7 available, and links a NEWS changelog and a GitHub repository. It shows no release dates or last-commit date, and I did not follow those links, so I cannot confirm whether it is actively maintained.
brief.caveats: The homepage gives no install instructions, platform list, or licence, and no usage examples. Bug reports go to a mailing list rather than an issue tracker. I did not reach the manual or the GitHub repository because the homepage gave no direct URLs for them. The scout note about LDAP being met mainly through identity systems is my reader's opinion, not from the project.

entry.title: ldapvi
entry.tldr: ldapvi pulls entries from an LDAP directory into your text editor and writes your edits back on save, like vipw for LDAP.
entry.deeper_look:
ldapvi is an interactive LDAP client for Unix terminals. You point it at a directory, it fetches the entries you ask for and opens them in your editor. You change the text, save, and the differences are sent back to the server.

The homepage sums it up in one line: "Think of it as vipw(1) for LDAP." vipw is the old Unix tool for editing the password file in a normal editor, with a safety net around it. ldapvi applies the same idea to a directory server. A live directory entry becomes something you edit like a file, rather than something you change through an admin GUI or a string of separate LDAP operations.

The idea underneath is that a protocol most developers only meet through login and identity systems has a plain, readable shape. Entries are names with attributes and values. Seeing them as text in your own editor is a quick way to learn what a directory holds and how it is structured.
entry.install:
brew install ldapvi
# you need access to an LDAP server to do anything useful with it
